newsitem.title: UK: UK banks cushioned against EMU forex jolt - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK banks cushioned against EMU forex jolt - survey.

text.p: The launch of a single European currency will deprive some European banks of up to 30 percent of foreign exchange revenues, but British banks will be cushioned against the blow by the global scale of their operations, a management constancy report said.

Datamonitor said only 12 percent of the turnover in London's foreign exchange market consisted of trades between other EU countries. This produced 360 million pounds ($590 million) profit per year but only about a fifth of this loss would be borne by UK banks, its report said.

This loss to the British banking industry assumes that all 15 EU countries participate," a press release on the report said. "However, this is an unlikely scenario. EMU will probably only encompass between six and eight of these countries in the initial stages, and thus forex revenue losses will be even smaller.

France and Portugal would be the largest sufferers from an irrevocable fixing of exchange rates, according to Datamonitor, as they could lose a substantial proportion of the 20 percent of trading undertaken between their currencies and the mark.
Many deals between peripheral European currencies are currently conducted via the U.S. dollar. The loss of this trade would also affect banks.
However, it can be argued that the market may well continue to do the same level of business as it does at present, but with the emerging market currencies instead, Datamonitor said.
The successful banks will try to branch out into dealing with emerging market currencies, author of the report, Kartik Natarajan, said.
